verdict.rationale: HumanLayer documents turning reported issues from GitHub, Linear, and Jira into agent tasks. It runs Claude Code or Codex sessions on those tasks, offers a Oneshot workflow for small clear changes, can run non-interactive sessions via `humanlayer automation run`, and can have the agent open a draft PR. Together these approximate an issue-to-fix pipeline. However, no evidence explicitly describes bug diagnosis, and the coding autonomy comes from the third-party agent harness HumanLayer orchestrates. missing for 10: explicit documentation of autonomous bug diagnosis/root-causing, an end-to-end evidenced bug-fix flow from issue to verified fix, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have an agent autonomously diagnose and fix a reported bug

citations.quote: Connect GitHub to create HumanLayer tasks from issues and link task artifacts back to the source issue.
A clear and small change can use Oneshot.
Use `humanlayer automation run` to run one Cloud-visible coding session from any automation environment — a CI job, a cron machine, or a script on a server.
Ask the session agent to open a draft pull request from the GitHub tab or diff view.
